Didge — installing on macOS
===========================

Copy each format you want into its folder. These are user folders, so no
administrator password is needed.

  Didge.vst3       ->  ~/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3/
  Didge.component  ->  ~/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/Components/
  Didge.clap       ->  ~/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/CLAP/
  Didge.app        ->  /Applications/   (or anywhere; it needs no host)

Then restart your host so it rescans.


These builds are not signed or notarised

macOS will refuse to open them on the first attempt and say the developer
cannot be verified. That message means the download carries a quarantine flag,
not that anything is wrong with the files. To clear it, run this once in
Terminal after copying:

  xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine ~/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3/Didge.vst3
  xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine ~/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/Components/Didge.component
  xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine ~/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/CLAP/Didge.clap
  xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Didge.app

For the standalone app you can instead right-click it, choose Open, and
confirm once.

If Logic or GarageBand still will not load the Audio Unit, check that it
passed validation:

  auval -v aumu Ddge Dtnv

Both Apple silicon and Intel are in the same binary, so there is one download
for either machine.

Building from source avoids all of the above, and is four commands. See
README.md.
